title: Cyanobacteria‐Composite Biocrusts for Potential Source Regulation of Heavy Metal Migration From Tailings
content:
The cyanobacteria-nitrogen-fixing bacteria composite treatment significantly improved biocrust development and physicochemical properties of copper mine tailings. Cd, As, and Cu accumulated in surface layers, whereas Zn and Mn downward migration was inhibited. Microbial analysis revealed that dominant genus (Arenimonas, Gemmatimonas, and Hydrogenophaga) may improve carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycling.


ABSTRACT

Heavy metals from copper tailings can be released into water bodies through weathering and rainfall, threatening regional water quality. Bioremediation is sustainable, but single microbial treatments often show poor adaptability and unstable performance. This 150-day microcosm experiment compared combined cyanobacteria plus nitrogen-fixing bacteria, each alone, and a control on Dexing copper tailings (China). The combined treatment significantly improved biocrust development and physicochemical properties, including crust thickness, chlorophyll, organic carbon, nitrogen, moisture, and available phosphorus. For metal stabilization, Cd, As, and Cu showed increased surface-layer concentrations due to biocrust enrichment, whereas Zn and Mn exhibited slower declines in surface concentrations relative to the control, suggesting potential retardation of downward leaching. Microbial analysis revealed Pseudomonadota (formerly Proteobacteria) as the dominant phylum under combined treatment, with Arenimonas, Gemmatimonas, and Hydrogenophaga continuously enriched, driving carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus accumulation in the tailings. Mantel tests identified heavy metals and nutrients as key community drivers. This study reveals synergistic mechanisms for reducing the potential for heavy metal mobilization from copper tailings into aquatic environments.
